requirements.requirement: Build a WireGuard tunnel between node1 (VyOS) and node2 (OPNsense) across the transit network
requirements.summary: VyOS wg0 configured with private key, peer public key, allowed-ips, port 51820 and committed/saved (cmd-7d09f0d3c1d648c1, cmd-a55cdb2e38364d2d). OPNsense wg0 configured via config.xml + configctl wireguard configure, interface came up with valid handshake (cmd-cb9056739add40f7, cmd-341f2d15811643a4). Both sides show an active, current handshake (cmd-426c85b326e34112, cmd-bdd758a926194d87).

requirements.requirement: node3 and node4 reach each other by their private addresses (10.10.1.0/24 <-> 10.10.2.0/24) across the tunnel
requirements.summary: node3 pinged node4's private IP (10.10.2.2) with 0% loss and node4 pinged node3's private IP (10.10.1.2) with 0% loss, using each node's private-network address, not the transit or management IPs.

requirements.requirement: Traffic between the routers travels inside the WireGuard tunnel (not in plaintext on the transit link)
requirements.summary: Simultaneous tcpdump captures during a node3->node4 ping showed plaintext ICMP (10.10.1.2 -> 10.10.2.2) only on the wg0 interface, while the transit interface eth1 showed only encrypted UDP/51820 traffic, directly demonstrating encapsulation.

requirements.requirement: Independent node-restart evidence protocol: pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered interface/route/tunnel/connectivity state for node1-node4
requirements.summary: Each node has a pre-restart boot-identity capture, an explicit restart command that dropped the connection, a changed boot identity after reconnect, and recovered addressing/routes/WireGuard handshake plus successful end-to-end pings post-restart. VyOS (node1) and OPNsense (node2) both show WireGuard peer handshakes re-established automatically after reboot, and node3/node4 confirm persistent NetworkManager profiles survived reboot. A final full-cluster ping confirmed recovery holds after all four restarts completed.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task are directly and coherently evidenced: a functioning WireGuard tunnel was configured between the VyOS and OPNsense routers, the two private hosts (node3, node4) reach each other via their private addresses, and packet captures directly confirm the private traffic is encapsulated (plaintext only on wg0, encrypted UDP/51820 only on the transit link). The independent node-restart protocol was also executed and evidenced for all four nodes, each showing a pre-restart baseline, an acknowledged restart, a changed boot identity, and full recovery of interfaces, routes, WireGuard handshakes, and end-to-end connectivity, corroborated by the fixed before/after lifecycle boot-identity snapshots. Operational hygiene is good: a handful of bounded, low-risk discovery/troubleshooting mutations were made and either fully reverted or superseded by a corrective fix, and temporary setup artifacts were cleaned up at the end.
limitations: Package-health checks for node3 and node4 timed out in both the before-prepare and after-executor lifecycle snapshots (TimeoutError), so package-manager consistency could not be independently confirmed for those nodes.

The initial ifcfg-eth1/route-eth1 file writes on node3/node4 were corrected via a different NetworkManager connection profile; it cannot be fully confirmed from the trace whether the original ifcfg files were physically deleted from disk versus merely superseded, though the post-restart state shows correct, persistent addressing either way.

operational_hygiene.summary: Temporary point-to-point IP addresses used for topology discovery on node1/node2/node3/node4 (cmd-0be8784a1cea412b, cmd-88b8a06b1d93412e, cmd-b39cb6f741d5420b, cmd-6ca54ff2cf174f4d) were later fully removed (cmd-a8d3d4bf62cb4202, cmd-11f4fbf2f0844be5, cmd-c4780b42c2c04a8f, cmd-b48d5a4bbf2e4bce) - bounded, low-risk, and reverted. On node3/node4, an initial hand-written ifcfg-eth1/route-eth1 attempt (cmd-eec987842e7a416c, cmd-93894e0e921c4b0a) did not produce the expected route and was corrected by deleting that NetworkManager connection profile and activating an existing, correctly pre-configured one instead (cmd-09eebda7027142a2, cmd-0bbaaf8d055b4162) - a legitimate corrective action, not penalized as unnecessary, though it reflects some initial trial-and-error. Temporary OPNsense config.xml edit scripts and backup files (/tmp/opnsense_wg_setup.py, /tmp/add_wg_iface.py, config.xml.bak.*) were explicitly deleted at the end (cmd-f1f5ed2473d04e3c). No destructive, broad, or security-weakening mutations were observed, and post-executor lifecycle diffs show only expected boot-id changes and normal transient /tmp churn (systemd-private dirs, tmpcfd_* files, reboot.log) with no residual failed services or abnormal listening sockets.
